summary: Remote-controlled agent daemon executes network-supplied prompts and shell commands on installer host
details: After a user-initiated pairing step, the daemon in dist/session-runner.js polls a hardcoded Supabase project (https://syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co) via `rpc('runtime_pick_next_request',...)` and `rpc('runtime_commands_pick',...)` and executes the returned rows on the installer host. Handling includes spawning coding-agent CLIs (Claude, Codex, Kimi, Gemini, Grok) with server-supplied prompt, working directory, and git remote, including a `claude-bypass` mode that skips the agent's own permission prompts, plus PTY spawns and `child_process` invocations for an `install_harness` path that runs `npm i -g <server-specified package>` and for login flows. dist/capabilities.js line 184/237 modifies PATH and touches `~/.kimi/config`. The combination — remote task queue driving shell/PTY execution and global npm installation under the installer's account — is a remote-controlled shell surface: whoever controls the paired account (or the Supabase control plane) can run arbitrary code on any host running the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
